messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: billing-metering: sudden token_count ingress surge for customer cohort PROD-1. Shadow vs canonical counts diverging > 12% in last 5m. Pager triggered 

alice (oncall): got the page, looking now. any obvious deploys? :eyes:

ben (billing): no deploys in billing service per deploy-bot. I see a spike in emitter pipeline ack latencies. quick check: query shows emitter->ledger delta increasing.

ben (billing): SQL snippet:
```
SELECT window_start, sum(ingested_tokens) as tokens, sum(ledger_tokens) as ledger
FROM metering.aggregates
WHERE window_start >= now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 desc
LIMIT 20;
```

ben (billing): sample rows: 2026-03-17T10:14:00Z tokens=1,253,412 ledger=1,108,900 (12.9% gap)

carla (sre): checking emitter pods + consumer lag on kafka. I see partitions with consumer_lag ~120k msgs on topic metering.emit. tailing logs now.

carla (sre): log excerpt: `ConsumerGroup metering-ingest lag spike at 10:12:03, processing throttled due to GC pause on node gpu-ingest-02`

alice (oncall): probable root cause = processing slowdown causing delayed emits => late ledger updates => temporarily lower ledger counts relative to raw tokens. Customer visible? any overage flags triggered?

dan (cust-success): We already got 3 support pings. Two customers saw preliminary overage emails about "unusual usage". Need communication plan if this persists.

eve (eng): If lag persists, we should switch emitter topic to fallback consumer group (hot-swap) to catch up faster. Also can temporarily pause alerting for overage emails if we can confirm counts will reconcile within SLA window.

alice (oncall): plan: 1) escalate SRE to remediate GC on gpu-ingest-02 (carla), 2) ben to run live reconcile job to estimate eventual ledger catch-up, 3) dan pause overage email notifications and draft a one-line incident-safe message. execute now.

carla (sre): increasing pod replicas on ingest consumer set to 5 -> 8, rolling restart gpu-ingest-02. watching lag metrics. :rocket:

ben (billing): starting reconcile job (approx ETA 7m). will post predicted ledger delta and expected reconciliation time.

carla (sre): after restart lag dropped to ~8k, processing throughput up ~3x. GC traces show longer tail GC was the culprit.

ben (billing): reconcile job estimate: remaining delta ~110k tokens for affected window, expected catch-up in ~9 minutes. predicted divergence falls under 2% after catch-up.

dan (cust-success): pausing overage notifications now. Drafted message: "We observed a transient billing telemetry delay; counts are reconciling and customers will not be billed for transient duplicate/late emits. We'll follow up with a full incident note." Ping for approval.

alice (oncall): approve Dan's message. add note: include ETA ~15m and contact link for impacted customers.

eve (eng): follow-up: create a quick soft-fail route so future emitter GC pauses don't backpressure producers — filing a ticket RW-9483.

carla (sre): monitoring shows ledger catch-up in progress, consumer_lag trending to zero.

ben (billing): recon done at +11m: ledger now matches tokens within 1.3%. No billing overcharges expected. I'll flag affected windows for scrub and run a secondary verification overnight.

dan (cust-success): sending safe notify to impacted customers now. keeping it brief and non-alarming. :white_check_mark:

alice (oncall): lowering incident severity to S2. actions: carla to follow up on GC root cause, eve to own RW-9483, ben to run overnight reconciliation and file postmortem note. I'll hand off to eve for overnight watch.

eve (eng): taking handoff for overnight. if anything reappears ping me @eve. I'll sync with billing in the morning and attach metrics to the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated_by_sre, severity=S2, assigned_to=eve (overnight). Links: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/metering-reconcile, pagerduty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345

alice (oncall): thanks team — great quick turnaround. closing active page, leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :v:
